This high-catalyst/high-substrate experiment produced more discrimination! Mechanisms now split more clearly:

Still good: M2, M19, M18, M8, M10, M15, M1, M13, M16, M17, M6, M14.

To discriminate these, I need:
- Low catalyst to separate dimerization models (M2, M13, M19) from non-dimerization ones.
- Long conversion to probe deactivation kinetics (M14, M16, M17, M18, M19).
</reflection>

<hypothesis>

- At low [cat], dimerization terms (M2, M13, M19) become insignificant → separating them from baseline M1 if they fit best due to dimerization.
- Substrate-involved deactivation (M16, M18) depends on S/catS concentrations; with high S and low cat, these effects manifest differently than in run_3.
- With some P present, we can test M17 (P+catS→dead) vs M14 (catS→dead) separately.

Use S = 2.0, cat = 0.002, P = 0.1. This is a completely different regime from prior runs.
</hypothesis>
